day_shape: 40 items dominated by tier-4 Iranian claims of coordinated missile strikes on US bases in Kuwait, Jordan and Bahrain, Iran International reporting a seventh night of US strikes on southern Iran, and Khamenei messaging on regional bases; nothing from UK Parliament, State Dept, OFAC or IAEA.

threads.label: Iranian claims of strikes on US Gulf bases
threads.summary: Regime outlets published multiple items claiming Iranian missile hits on US positions at Muwaffaq al-Salti (Jordan), Sheikh Isa (Bahrain) and sites in Kuwait, with Defa Press citing satellite imagery of a destroyed aircraft shelter. Jerusalem Post reported sirens and interceptions accompanying the claimed coordinated attacks, and Defa Press cited Fox News saying 13 US personnel had been wounded.

threads.label: Reported US strikes on southern Iran
threads.summary: Iran International reported a seventh consecutive night of US strikes destroying bridges, tunnels and rail links across southern Iran and severing roads to the Strait of Hormuz coast. Defa Press claimed multiple US missile attacks on Sirik in Hormozgan at 12:30, 16:30 and 16:40 with no civilian casualties reported, while Foreign Ministry spokesman Baghaei posted images of eight people said to have been killed in 26 July strikes.

threads.label: Tehran messaging on Hormuz and retaliation
threads.summary: Khamenei's office said regional lands would no longer serve as a shield for US bases, while IRIB disputed CENTCOM's statement that the Strait of Hormuz was open and MP Kousari told Defa Press that management of the strait was entirely in Iran's hands. A security official cited by Defa Press warned that Dubai and Abu Dhabi airports should be evacuated if the US struck Iranian infrastructure, and lawmakers pushed continued 'blood vengeance' discourse.

threads.label: Gaza, Lebanon and Israel coverage
threads.summary: IRIB reported nine Palestinians killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza including five in the al-Nasser neighbourhood, and Defa Press said Israeli air, drone and artillery strikes on southern Lebanon continued around Nabatieh. A Jerusalem Post opinion piece called for resettling Gaza, and Defa Press flagged Belgium's ban on imports from Palestinian occupied territories.

threads.label: Postponed leader commemoration and Arbaeen logistics
threads.summary: The Office of the First Vice President announced that the 28 July ceremony at Imam Khomeini prayer ground to commemorate the 'martyred leader of the Islamic Revolution' had been cancelled and postponed. Separately, Iran's passport police said over 520,000 Arbaeen pilgrimage passports had been issued in Muharram and outlined remote application and border readiness measures.

events.summary_en: Unprecedented decline in US reserves makes price increases inevitable - US economist Chris Martenson: We are facing a major risk here. US petrol and diesel reserves at this point in the year have never been this low. Despite this, the US continues to export in order to keep prices down for other parts of the world; at the expense of pressure on American citizens. One cannot keep fuel reserves this low and expect that prices won't increase significantly at some point.

events.title_en: Land borders fully prepared to welcome Arbaeen pilgrims
events.summary_en: Land borders fully prepared to welcome Arbaeen pilgrims. Head of the Arbaeen central headquarters in discussion with news network: Khosravi border is one of the best borders in terms of facilities and amenities for Arbaeen pilgrims. Pilgrims from central and north-western provinces of the country can use Khosravi border for transit. Sumar border in Gilangharb city this year will be readied for operation on a pilot basis. Possibility of limited transit of indigenous people through Sumar border will be provided in the form of pilot caravans.
